body.title: docs(auth): recommend glab as Git credential helper on OAuth-only instances
body.description:
## Description

On GitLab instances where personal access tokens are disabled, users cannot generate access tokens manually for Git over HTTPS operations. Users often configure Git Credential Manager by registering a separate personal OAuth application and secret on the instance.

`glab auth login --setup-git-credential-helper` configures `glab` as a host-scoped Git credential helper. It uses `glab`'s existing OAuth application and refreshes tokens automatically.

This MR updates the documentation and login command help text to:

- Recommend `glab auth login --setup-git-credential-helper` (and `glab auth login --web --setup-git-credential-helper`) on OAuth-only instances.
- Explain that using `glab` avoids creating a separate OAuth application.
- Clarify when `glab` can replace Git Credential Manager.

## Related Issues

related to #8701

## How has this been tested?

I verified the command help and documentation text against the CLI documentation style guide, and verified wording with the wording lint.

The rest runs in the pipeline.

Implemented with AI assistance; I reviewed and tested the changes.

body.title: fix(release): report a failed close and remove a partial asset
body.description:
Re-lands !3562 by @ihopenre-eng on current `main`, since that MR went stale with conflicts. The commit keeps them as author.

`glab release download` dropped the error from closing the asset file and left a partial file behind when a download failed, so the next attempt failed with "file exists". The close error is now returned, and the file is removed on any failure.

<details>
<summary>Changes from !3562</summary>

- Resolved the conflict with the `url.Parse` check and the Markdown-upload download path that landed on `main` after !3562 was opened. The deferred cleanup covers both.
- `Test_downloadAsset_RemovesPartialFileOnErrorStatus` is now table-driven and also covers the Markdown-upload path. Both cases fail with the `os.Remove` disabled.
- A failed `os.Remove` is joined into the returned error, so a file that could not be cleaned up is reported instead of silently left behind.
- Squashed the three commits into one and trimmed the comments.

Not covered by tests: the close-error half. Making `*os.File.Close` fail would need an interface seam, which is out of proportion for this change.

</details>

Closes #8429

body.title: feat(deploy-token): Add the create command
body.description:
## Description

Third of four merge requests implementing `glab deploy-token` for #8062, after !3879 (`list`) and !4193 (`get`). This one adds the `create` subcommand, for both project and group deploy tokens.

`revoke` follows.

### Command surface

```plaintext
glab deploy-token create <name> -S, --scope <scope>... [--username <username>] [-E, --expires-at <date>] [-g, --group <group>] [-F, --output text|json] [--jq <expr>] [-R, --repo <repo>]
```

`--scope` is the only required flag. `-S` and `-E` are the shorthands `glab token create` already uses for the same two concepts.

### Notes for review

- **This is the one command whose output carries the token value.** `list` and `get` clear `Token` before printing; `create` must not, because this is the only response GitLab ever returns it in. The two tests that pin this are deliberate mirrors of the withholding tests in the other two packages, so the inversion is asserted rather than assumed.
- **`mcpannotations.Exclude`, not `Safe`.** The command prints a secret, so it is kept out of the MCP surface exactly as `glab token create` is. `Safe` would be wrong even though creating a token is not destructive.
- **The detail rows match `get`, minus the two that cannot be interesting.** Same `tableprinter` vertical layout, same first five labels in the same order, with `Token` appended last as the value to copy. `Revoked` and `Expired` are dropped: a token that was just created is neither, so printing `false` twice would be noise.
- **Scopes are not validated in `glab`.** The API documentation lists different scope sets for the project and group endpoints, with the virtual registry scopes documented as project-only. Against GitLab.com the group endpoint accepted `read_virtual_registry`, so a client-side allowlist built from that table would have rejected a request GitLab honours. The accepted set also depends on which features an instance has enabled. The command therefore passes `--scope` through and lets GitLab answer, and the help text links to the scope list rather than restating it.
- **`--expires-at` uses `pflag`'s own `TimeVar`.** `internal/commands/mr/list` and `internal/commands/issuable/list` already use it; this is the same helper with `time.DateOnly` added alongside `time.RFC3339`, since a deploy token expiry is a date in the UI and the API's own examples use `YYYY-MM-DD`. `pflag` produces the format error itself and names both layouts in it, so no parsing or message handling is needed here.
- **An omitted flag is sent as nil, not as an empty value.** `expires_at` and `username` are both optional in the API, where absent means "never expires" and "assign the default username". Sending a zero time or an empty string would be a different request, so neither field is set unless the flag was given. The tests assert both the nil and the populated case.
- **The advisory goes to stderr, and only in text mode.** `--output json` is what a script reads, so that path emits nothing but the API response; `--jq .token` yields a bare token value with no extra line to strip.
- **File completion is disabled**, as it is for `list` and `get`.

### Commits

- **feat(deploy-token): Add the create command**

  Issuing a deploy token still required the web UI, which left CI/CD
  setup only half-scriptable now that list and get exist.

## Related Issues

Related to #8062.

Not `Resolves`, deliberately: this is the third of four merge requests in the series, and the issue should stay open until `revoke` lands.

## How has this been tested?

**Unit tests** - `internal/commands/deploy-token/create/create_test.go`, using `cmdtest.SetupCmdForTest` with client-go mocks from `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3/testing`. No `httpmock` responders. The mock captures the options struct the command sends, so the tests assert on the request and not only on what is printed: the name, the parsed scopes, and whether `Username` and `ExpiresAt` are nil or populated. Covers project scope, group scope, `--output json` keeping the token value, the three ways of passing scopes, a custom username, both accepted expiry layouts, a rejected expiry, `--scope` being required, an API error, `--repo` with `--group` being rejected, and both sides of the base repository requirement. Coverage of the package is 94.7%.

**Against a real instance** - run against a project and a group, with every token created by these runs deleted afterwards. Token values are redacted below:

```shell
$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-1 --scope read_repository -R <project>
ID	16716190
Name	glab-r3-1
Username	gitlab+deploy-token-16716190
Scopes	read_repository
Expires At	-
Token	gldt-<redacted>
! Store the token value now. It is not shown again.

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-2 --scope read_repository,read_registry --username glab-r3-user --expires-at 2027-12-31 -R <project>
ID	16716192
Name	glab-r3-2
Username	glab-r3-user
Scopes	read_repository, read_registry
Expires At	2027-12-31T00:00:00Z
Token	gldt-<redacted>
! Store the token value now. It is not shown again.

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-3 --scope read_repository -R <project> -F json
{"id":16716197,"name":"glab-r3-3","username":"gitlab+deploy-token-16716197","expires_at":null,"revoked":false,"expired":false,"token":"gldt-<redacted>","scopes":["read_repository"]}

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-4 --scope read_repository -R <project> -F json --jq .token
gldt-<redacted>

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-5 --scope read_repository -g <group>
ID	16716199
Name	glab-r3-5
Username	gitlab+deploy-token-16716199
Scopes	read_repository
Expires At	-
Token	gldt-<redacted>
! Store the token value now. It is not shown again.
```

A date-only expiry round-trips as `2027-12-31T00:00:00Z`, and the default username is `gitlab+deploy-token-<id>`, both confirmed above.

The rejected inputs. These render lowercase because !4141 stopped fang title-casing the first word, so error text now appears as written:

```shell
$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-bad --scope not_a_scope -R <project>
POST https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/<project>/deploy_tokens: 400 {error: scopes does not have a valid value}.

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-bad -R <project>
required flag(s) "scope" not set.

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-bad --scope read_repository --expires-at tomorrow -R <project>
invalid argument "tomorrow" for "-E, --expires-at" flag: invalid time format `tomorrow` must be one of: `2006-01-02`, `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00`.
Try --help for usage.

$ glab deploy-token create glab-r3-bad --scope read_repository -R <project> -g <group>
if any flags in the group [repo group] are set none of the others can be; [group repo] were all set.

$ cd /tmp && glab deploy-token create glab-r3-bad --scope read_repository
not a git repository: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

Shell completion was checked to confirm the argument offers no filenames:

```shell
$ glab __complete deploy-token create ""
:4
Completion ended with directive: ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp
```

`lefthook run pre-push` passes in full, including `comment-overlap`, `comment-ratio`, `check-generated`, `check-args`, `markdownlint`, `vale` and `lychee`.

## Screenshots (if appropriate):

N/A - the command is terminal output only, shown above.

body.title: perf(mr view): skip fields and approval state the output doesn't use
body.description:
Closes #8674

## What

- Send `include_diverged_commits_count`, `render_html` and `include_rebase_in_progress` only with `--output json`. Text output doesn't use them, and the diverged commits count needs a Gitaly call.
- Call `GetApprovalState` only for the TTY preview. JSON and raw output never used it.

## Tests

`TestMRView_requestsPerOutputMode` covers TTY, raw, JSON in a TTY, and JSON without one. Each case checks the options passed to the merge request `GET` and whether `approval_state` is requested. All four cases fail against the old code.

## Manual test

Built `main` and this branch, and ran both against gitlab.com on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4253 and https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/162448 (152,881 commits behind its target, a worst case for the diverged commits count).

| Mode | Requests before | Requests after |
|---|---|---|
| TTY | `GET` with 3 options + `approval_state` | `GET` + `approval_state` |
| Raw | `GET` with 3 options + `approval_state` | `GET` |
| `--output json` | `GET` with 3 options + `approval_state` | `GET` with 3 options |

Raw and JSON output are byte-identical. TTY output differs only in the "opened N minutes ago" timestamp.

## Performance

Median wall time of `glab mr view`, 15 alternating runs per binary:

| MR | Mode | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cli!4253 | TTY | 1226 ms | 1197 ms | −2% |
| cli!4253 | Raw | 1371 ms | 751 ms | −45% |
| cli!4253 | JSON | 1208 ms | 676 ms | −44% |
| gitlab!162448 | TTY | 1948 ms | 1574 ms | −19% |
| gitlab!162448 | Raw | 1909 ms | 659 ms | −65% |
| gitlab!162448 | JSON | 1897 ms | 763 ms | −60% |

- Most of the saving is the dropped `approval_state` request. On the large project it's slower than the merge request `GET` itself (1123 ms against 571 ms median, through `glab api`).
- The three options add about 50 to 120 ms at the median, and about 450 ms at p90 on the stale MR.
- JSON output is unchanged but also gets faster, because it no longer sends `approval_state`.

Local timings, so approximate. After release, compare versions in Kibana as described in the issue.

body.title: fix(mr): show the real total in the mr issues header
body.description:
## Description

`glab mr issues` discarded the `*gitlab.Response` from
`GetIssuesClosedOnMerge`, so the header only reported the number of rows it
received. The command sends no pagination options, so the API returns its
default page of 20. For a merge request that closes 25 issues, the header read
`Showing 20 issues in <project> that match your search.`, with nothing to show
that 5 more exist.

This keeps the response and passes `resp.TotalItems` to the list title, the
same approach as !4215 (`cluster agent list`):

- The header reads, for example,
  `Showing 20 of 25 issues in <project> that match your search.`
- When the response carries no total, the header stays as it is today.

`GET /projects/:id/merge_requests/:merge_request_iid/closes_issues` paginates
its result (`paginate(issues)` in `lib/api/merge_requests.rb`), so `X-Total`
is present.

Only the header line changes. The table is unchanged.

`mr issues` has no `--page` or `--per-page` flags, so issues past the first 20
still can't be listed. That would add new flags rather than fix the header, so
I've left it out of this MR. I'm happy to open a follow-up if that's wanted.

## Related Issues

Closes #8654

Related to #1165

## How has this been tested?

- Added `TestMergeRequestClosesIssues_HeaderTotal` in
  `internal/commands/mr/issues/mr_issues_test.go`, with a case that returns
  `TotalItems: 25` and expects
  `Showing 1 of 25 issues in OWNER/REPO that match your search. `, and a case
  without a total that keeps `Showing 1 issue ...`. It compares the first line
  with `assert.Equal`. The case with a total fails without this change.
- `go test ./internal/commands/mr/issues/` passes.
- `go vet ./internal/commands/mr/issues/` passes.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/commands/mr/issues/` (v2.14.0) reports 0
  issues, and `golangci-lint fmt --diff` reports no changes.
- `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap` reports no findings in the changed files.
- Ran a build of this branch and a build of `main` against a local
  `gitlab/gitlab-ce:19.2.6-ce.0` container, with a merge request whose
  description closes 25 issues:

  | Command | `main` | This branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `glab mr issues 1` | `Showing 20 issues in root/mr-issues-test that match your search.` | `Showing 20 of 25 issues in root/mr-issues-test that match your search.` |

  Both builds list the same 20 rows, and the table body is byte-identical to
  `main`.

body.title: chore: let gitlab-bot approve docs changes
body.description:
## What

Follow-up to !4194. Adds `@gitlab-bot` as a Code Owner of `/docs/` and `README.md`, alongside the maintainers and `@gl-docsteam`.

This expands the scope agreed in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8575, which kept documentation with its existing owners.

## Why

A command change usually edits `Short`, `Long`, `Example` or flag descriptions, and `make gen-docs` regenerates the pages under `docs/source/` and the command list in `README.md` in the same commit. Those files need a maintainer or technical writer, so most command MRs can't take the Duo-only path even when the change is code. Example: !4153.

## Not changed

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, agent, policy, security, CI and release files stay with humans.
- Docs lint config (`docs/.vale/`, `docs/.rumdl/rumdl.toml`, `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`) keeps tw-docops and tw-leadership as owners.
- Team-delegated docs (`govern/`, `orbit/`, `dependency-firewall/`) keep their owners: their later patterns replace the `/docs/` owners. Adding the bot there is for those teams to decide, as with their code paths.

Relates to https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8575
